title: Urgent Zoho Healthcare CRM Automation & Deluge Fix

facts: Post: small urgent healthcare automation inside an existing Zoho CRM setup; review the patient/lead workflow.

Post asks: task on new patient/enquiry record, status update on conditions, internal notification to the assigned user, a small Deluge function for field validation/update, a guard against running twice on the same record, testing with sample records and a short explanation of the logic.
No person or business name in the post; client reviews name no contact. Account shown as 'Your team'.
Every patient, coordinator and record in the deck is invented. No health details are used.

cover.beat: Here's how your patient enquiry follow-up would work in Zoho. A new enquiry comes in, gets checked and cleaned, the right coordinator gets a callback task and an alert, and saving the record again doesn't set it off a second time.

scenes.title: What happens when a new enquiry is created
scenes.caption: Rosa asks for a new patient visit on your website. The workflow checks it hasn't run on her record, cleans her details, then creates the task.
scenes.beat: Follow Rosa through it. Her enquiry is created. First the workflow checks that it hasn't already run on this record and ticks a box so it can't run again. A small Deluge function cleans up her phone and email. Then Jordan gets a callback task, the status moves to callback scheduled, and Jordan gets an alert.
details: The run-once check comes first, so nothing else fires on a record that has already been handled.
If the phone number doesn't pass the check, the status becomes Needs contact check instead, and no callback task is created.
Use Replay to play the steps in order, or Show result to jump to the end.

scenes.beat: Now the run-twice test. At 9:52 we edit Rosa's record and save it again. The workflow sees the box is already ticked and stops right there. Jordan still has one callback task and one alert, not two.
details: I'd also test a record with a bad phone number to check the Needs contact check path.
